what: EXACT-REPRODUCTION TESTS MUST PIN OR RECORD THE RUNNER CLASS. MEASURED 2026-11-06 (timeframe units b620..b626, one data pin, identical fold sizes): the in-unit 1h baseline took exactly TWO outcomes across five runner runs, each reproduced exactly (so deterministic, not noise). Class A = round 1 exactly, n 71,950/71,886/72,063 and seed-mean +0.0089486 (runs 42130510691 b620, 42162879141 b626). Class B = n 71,917/71,882/72,071 and +0.007953 (runs 42157944198 b625, 42165663948 b622, 42167537521 b624; three runs, identical values). The cause is a runner or library-build dependence of the LightGBM fit; a CPU-class dependence is the hypothesis, UNVERIFIED because the run manifests recorded nothing about the runner. Any rule of the form 'reproduces within tol of X' or 'ship fit A only if its sha matches' (the equity export RQ-20261106-e9a1-03 does exactly this) is therefore runner dependent. DONE in this lane: scripts/research/runner_fingerprint.py, recorded as run-manifest.json 'runner' (shared by every research-script-run unit) and in the timeframe results (cpu model and SIMD flags, cores, OS image, python and numpy/lightgbm/pandas/scipy/sklearn versions, BLAS, and a short class_id hash). OPEN: (1) after the first runs that carry it, test the hypothesis: does class_id separate class A runs from class B runs? (2) per reproduction rule decide: pin the class (require the same class_id) or compare within a class; (3) audit existing exact-reproduction and sha-match rules for this dependence.
